newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North says Alumbrera financing drawn down.
newsitem.headline: North says Alumbrera financing drawn down.

text.p: Mining house North Ltd said on Thursday that the first draw-down of project financing for Argentina's Alumbrera copper and gold mine project took place on July 30.
North and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd each have a 25 percent stake in the project and Australia's MIM Holdings Ltd owns 50 percent.

It said the limited recourse project financing totals US$670 million of which US$542 million was underwritten by a group of banks led by Citibank NA. International syndication of the financing ended recently and was oversubscribed.
Other banks in the lead group included co-lead managers and underwriters ABN Amro, ANZ Bank, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Dresdner Bank.
North said the remainder of the US$128 million in project financing was provided by the German long term investment bank Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau (KfW).

This contribution consisted of US$100 million based on long-term delivery of copper concentrate to a German smelter and a US$28 million export loan tied to German export contracts for goods and services.
